title: Una the Unicorn Learns to Glow Softly
markdown:
In the heart of the Meadow of Whispering Willows, where the grass grew as soft as a dandelion puff and the flowers whispered secrets only to the gentlest of breezes, lived a unicorn foal named Una. Her coat shimmered with rainbow colors, like the inside of a seashell. Her mane was the soft, dusky color of summer twilight. But Una had a special feature: her glow. It wasn't a bright, sudden light. It was a gentle, steady radiance that pulsed from her. It was like a sunbeam woven with starlight. This soft glow made her delicate hooves seem to float just above the clover. Her slender horn twinkled with the promise of happy dreams.

As the sun, a big golden ball, began to dip below the rolling hills, painting the sky in beautiful shades of orange, pink, and purple, Una’s magical glow became a bit too much for a sleepy evening. The fireflies, who usually blinked their cheerful greetings across the darkening meadow, found their tiny lanterns completely outshone. They tried to blink their little lights, to send their usual signals, but Una’s steady glow was always there, a bright beacon.

“Oh, Una,” buzzed Barnaby Beetle, his voice a tiny, sleepy drone. “Your glow is ever so lovely, truly it is, but it’s quite hard to get a proper wink when you’re as bright as a midday moon.”

The little field mice, who normally would have been tucked snugly in their cozy homes, their whiskers twitching with sleep, found themselves wide awake. “It’s a bit… well, *very* bright, Una,” squeaked Millie Mouse, her whiskers drooping with tiredness. Even Mrs. Rabbit, who could usually sleep through a passing thundercloud and a flock of squawking geese, found herself blinking her large, soft eyes open again and again. The gentle light from Una’s meadow was just too strong.

The whole forest seemed to let out a soft, sleepy sigh. Una looked down at her shimmery hooves, a little disappointed. Her starry mane drooped. She truly loved her glow; it was a part of her. But she didn’t want it to keep everyone else awake. It is known among the forest folk that a sleepy friend is often a grumbly friend, and that wouldn’t do at all.

Una tried with all her might to dim her own radiant light. She squeezed her eyes shut as tightly as a little bud closing for the night. She wished it would fade away. She even tried to hide behind a particularly large, striped toadstool, hoping its earthy cap might soak up some of her brightness. But her glow was as much a part of her as her own heartbeat, as essential as the stars in the night sky. It simply wouldn’t go out. She let out a tiny, frustrated puff of air through her nostrils. To her surprise, this only made her horn sparkle a little more.

Just then, as the first few shy stars, like tiny diamonds, began to appear in the deep blue sky, a slow, steady figure ambled into the clearing. It was Dobby, a donkey with a coat the color of warm earth after a gentle rain. His ears seemed to droop just so, as if they were listening to the very rhythm of the world. Dobby wasn’t known for his speed, but he was known for his wisdom. He moved with a deep calm that seemed to settle the very leaves on the ancient oak trees. He saw Una looking glum, her bright glow lighting up the worried little faces of her friends gathered around her.

Dobby observed the meadow for a quiet moment. The fireflies blinked, their light struggling. The mice twitched their noses, still awake. Then, Dobby spoke, his voice a low, gentle rumble, like distant thunder on a warm summer’s day. “Well now, little Una,” he said, his voice calming and clear. “You seem to have a bit too much sparkle for a sleepy evening, hmm?”

Una nodded, her starry mane drooping even further. “I can’t make it dim, Dobby! Everyone’s trying to sleep, but I’m just too bright. It’s like I’m a little sun, even when I want to be a sleepy moonbeam.”

Dobby nudged her gently with his soft nose, a gesture of comfort and understanding. “Ah, yes. The glow of a young unicorn is a powerful thing, indeed. It is like the sun, always wanting to shine its fullest light. But even the sun must have its rest, must it not? Consider this, Una: sometimes, to make something gentle, you must *breathe* gentle. Try this with me. Take a slow breath in, filling your chest like a little balloon being filled with the sweetest air.”

Una took a breath. For a fleeting moment, the glow around her pulsed with a little more brightness.

“Now,” Dobby continued patiently, his voice unwavering, “hold it, just for a whisper of a second, no longer than it takes a dewdrop to form. And then, let it out *ever* so slowly. Imagine you are blowing out a tiny, delicate candle, one wisp of air at a time. Let the air leave your lungs as slowly as a single, perfect snowflake drifting down from the sky.”

Una tried again, focusing with all her might. She breathed in, slowly and deeply. Then she exhaled, her breath a soft, contented sigh. As she exhaled, something magical happened. Her glow seemed to soften, as if a wispy cloud had drifted gently over the moon.

“That’s it!” Dobby encouraged, his ears perking up slightly. “Again. Slow breath in. And slow breath out. Feel your own quietness. Your own peace. Let it flow through you, from your heart to your hooves, and your light will surely follow. It is a song you sing with your breath.”

Una continued to breathe, her soft sighs mingling nicely with the gentle rustling of the leaves. With each slow, careful exhale, her radiant glow began to dim. It didn’t disappear entirely, of course; that would be like asking a star to stop twinkling or a river to stop flowing. But it softened, changing from a bright, strong radiance into a gentle halo. It felt like a warm hug rather than a bright lamp.

The fireflies blinked, and this time, their little lights shone clearly and brightly. Their signals were once again visible across the meadow. Millie Mouse yawned, a proper, deep, satisfied yawn. Her tiredness melted away. Mrs. Rabbit’s eyes fluttered shut, and soon a soft, contented snore could be heard, a gentle rhythm in the quiet night. The meadow settled into a peaceful hush. A blanket of calm descended upon the land. Una felt a lovely, soothing calmness spread through her whole being. She realized her glow wasn’t a problem to be fixed, but a beautiful magic to be understood and gently managed.

Una smiled, a soft, sleepy smile that radiated contentment. “Thank you, Dobby,” she whispered, her voice now as gentle and soft as the moonlight itself. “I can do it now. It feels so nice.”

Dobby gave a contented sigh, a sound like the earth breathing. “Patience now, little one. All will be revealed in time, with a gentle breath and a quiet heart. The stars themselves whisper this wisdom.”

And so, Una the unicorn foal learned that even the brightest magic can be softly managed, just like a song can be sung softly or a story can be told in a whisper. As the moon climbed high into the inky sky, casting long, sleepy shadows across the now peaceful meadow, the Meadow of Whispering Willows was finally quiet, filled with the gentle breaths and soft dreams of all its inhabitants. It was a peaceful scene, all thanks to a wise old donkey and a little unicorn who learned to breathe. The ancient trees remember this story well, and every night, as they sway gently in the breeze, they rustle their leaves in a soft reminder of the gentle magic that can bloom when we learn to breathe and listen to our own quiet heart.
characters: Una the unicorn foal, Dobby the donkey
